descripcion_es: Family relationships and describing people's appearance and personality.
resumen: Words to talk about family members and marital status, and to describe a person's appearance and personality.

explicacion.texto: In English there are different words for male and female, and sometimes one word for both: parents (father and mother; Spanish “padres”), siblings (brothers and sisters in general), grandparents. “Relatives” are the members of your family; “relations” means the same, but it is less common.

filas: male / female child of the same parents (es: hermano / hermana)
brothers and sisters, either sex (es: hermanos)
sons and daughters; young people (es: hijos, niños)
father / mother of a parent (es: abuelo / abuela)
brother / sister of a parent (es: tío / tía)
child of your uncle or aunt (es: primo / prima)
My cousin Pablo is a pilot.
son / daughter of your brother or sister (es: sobrino / sobrina)
married man / married woman (es: marido / mujer)
the person you live with or are in a relationship with (es: pareja)
man / woman you are going out with (es: novio / novia)
father of your spouse / sister of your spouse or wife of your brother (es: suegro / cuñada)
child with no brothers or sisters (es: hijo único)
of great / small height (es: alto / bajo)
light / dark hair colour (es: pelo rubio / moreno)
thin / too heavy (es: delgado / con sobrepeso)
My son is a bit shy.
works a lot / doesn't want to work (es: trabajador / vago)
be similar in appearance to (es: parecerse físicamente)
have a good relationship with (es: llevarse bien con)
I get on well with my cousins.

items: For hair and eyes, use have: She has got blue eyes and curly hair.
What is he like? asks about personality; What does he look like? asks about appearance.
Words with -in-law form the plural on the first word: sisters-in-law.

ejemplos.frase: I have one brother and no sisters.
ejemplos.traduccion: Tengo un hermano y ninguna hermana.

ejemplos.frase: My grandparents live in a small village.
ejemplos.traduccion: Mis abuelos viven en un pueblo pequeño.

ejemplos.frase: What's your sister like? – She's friendly and very funny.
ejemplos.traduccion: ¿Cómo es tu hermana? – Es simpática y muy graciosa.

ejemplos.frase: Everyone says I look like my mother.
ejemplos.traduccion: Todo el mundo dice que me parezco a mi madre.

ejemplos.frase: My nephew has got red hair and green eyes.
ejemplos.traduccion: Mi sobrino tiene el pelo pelirrojo y los ojos verdes.

ejemplos.frase: We get on very well with our neighbours.
ejemplos.traduccion: Nos llevamos muy bien con nuestros vecinos.

errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Father and mother together are parents; fathers means several fathers.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: I have two brothers: Ana and Luis.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: I have a sister and a brother: Ana and Luis.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Brothers are only male siblings; in general, siblings.

errores_hispanohablantes.mal: She is very educated with everybody.
errores_hispanohablantes.bien: She is very polite to everybody.
errores_hispanohablantes.nota: Spanish “educado” (courteous) is polite; educated means cultured, with a good education.

ejercicios.explicacion: According to the card's family table, uncle / aunt are the brother / sister of a parent. The clue is that this is a woman (sister) from the parents' generation: she is the aunt. The possessive form my mother's sister means “the sister of my mother” (the 's shows possession).
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Your mother's sister is your aunt.
ejercicios.traduccion: La hermana de mi madre es mi tía.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Uncle is the male relative; your mother's sister is a woman: aunt.
That is the Spanish word; in English it is aunt.
Ant is an insect; although in American English they sometimes sound the same, the relative is spelt aunt.

glosario.definicion_l: the sister of your father or mother; the wife of your uncle
the brother of your father or mother; the husband of your aunt · a source of help and advice and encouragement

ejercicios.explicacion: The card's table gives cousin for both Spanish “primo” and “prima”: the same word is used for both sexes. The clue is the relationship: the son of your uncle is your cousin. Unlike Spanish, you do not need to change the word for a female cousin.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Your uncle's son is your cousin.
ejercicios.traduccion: El hijo de mi tío es mi primo.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Nephew is the son of your brother or sister; your uncle's son is your cousin.
That is the Spanish word; in English it is cousin.
The correct spelling is cousin, with -ou-.

glosario.definicion_l: the child of your aunt or uncle
the divine word of God; the second person in the Trinity (incarnate in Jesus) · a male human offspring

ejercicios.explicacion: The card's table gives nephew / niece as the son / daughter of your brother or sister. The clue is that this is a girl (daughter) of the next generation, the daughter of a brother: she is the niece. Do not confuse it with nephew, the male form.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Your brother's daughter is your niece.
ejercicios.traduccion: La hija de mi hermano es mi sobrina.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Nephew is male; your brother's daughter is your niece.
Cousin is the child of your uncle or aunt; your brother's daughter is your niece.
A common spelling mistake: it is spelt niece (i before e).

glosario.definicion_l: a daughter of your brother or sister
a son of your brother or sister
a female human offspring

ejercicios.explicacion: The card's table gives father-in-law (Spanish “suegro”): relatives by marriage are formed by adding -in-law (sister-in-law). The clue is wife's father, the father of your spouse. It is written with hyphens and, as the card says, the plural goes on the first word (fathers-in-law).
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Your spouse's father is your father-in-law.
ejercicios.traduccion: El padre de mi mujer es mi suegro.

errores_previstos.explicacion: It is written with hyphens: father-in-law.
Stepfather is your mother's husband who is not your father, not your wife's father.
Grandfather is your parent's father; your wife's father is your father-in-law.

glosario.definicion_l: the father of your spouse
a married woman; a man's partner in marriage

ejercicios.frase: My ___ are both doctors: my father and my mother.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card's table gives parents as father and mother together. The clue is the final clarification, my father and my mother: it refers to both parents together. This is one of the typical mistakes on the card: fathers would be several male parents.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Father and mother together are parents.
ejercicios.traduccion: Mis padres son médicos los dos: mi padre y mi madre.

por_opcion.parents: Correct: parents = father and mother together.
por_opcion.fathers: Incorrect: fathers is the plural of father, several male parents; it does not include the mother.
por_opcion.relatives: Incorrect: relatives are family members in general (uncles, cousins…), not specifically your parents.

glosario.definicion_l: a father or mother; one who begets or one who gives birth to or nurtures and raises a child; a relative who plays the role of guardian · an organism (plant or animal) from which younger ones are obtained
estimated by comparison; not absolute or complete · properly related in size or degree or other measurable characteristics; usually followed by ‘to’
(used with count nouns) two considered together; the two

ejercicios.frase: I don't have any brothers or sisters. I'm an ___ child.
ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives only child (Spanish “hijo único”). The clue is the first sentence: he has no brothers or sisters. Here only means “single, the one” and goes before the noun; unique exists, but it means “exceptional, one of a kind” and does not form this expression. Note that we say an only child, with an because only begins with a vowel.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: A child with no siblings is an only child.
ejercicios.traduccion: No tengo hermanos. Soy hijo único.

por_opcion.only: Correct: only child = a child with no brothers or sisters.
por_opcion.alone: Incorrect: alone means “without company” and does not go before a noun.
por_opcion.unique: Incorrect: unique means “one of a kind, exceptional”; also, it would take a, not an.

glosario.definicion_l: isolated from others · lacking companions or companionship
radically distinctive and without equal · (followed by ‘to’) applying exclusively to a given category or condition or locality

ejercicios.enunciado: Choose the right question to ask for a physical description.
ejercicios.frase: ___ – He's tall with short grey hair.
ejercicios.explicacion: The list of rules and key points explains that What does he look like? asks about appearance and What is he like? asks about personality. The clue is the answer: tall with short grey hair describes physical appearance. How is he? asks about health or mood.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: What does he look like? asks about physical appearance.
ejercicios.traduccion: ¿Cómo es (físicamente)? – Es alto y tiene el pelo corto y canoso.

por_opcion.What does he look like?: Correct: it asks about physical appearance, which is what the answer describes.
por_opcion.What is he like?: Incorrect: it asks about character or personality; the answer would be friendly, shy, funny…
por_opcion.How is he?: Incorrect: it asks how he is (health or mood); the answer would be He's fine, thanks.

glosario.definicion_l: bear a physical resemblance to

ejercicios.frase: She never speaks in class. She's very ___.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card's second table gives shy: nervous with other people. The clue is the earlier description: someone who never speaks in class is shy. Funny and lazy describe other traits that cannot be deduced from the sentence.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Shy means nervous with other people (es: tímido).
ejercicios.traduccion: Nunca habla en clase. Es muy tímida.

por_opcion.shy: Correct: shy = nervous with other people.
por_opcion.funny: Incorrect: funny means “amusing, makes you laugh”; someone who doesn't speak is unlikely to seem funny.
por_opcion.lazy: Incorrect: lazy means “doesn't want to work”; it has nothing to do with not speaking in class.

glosario.definicion_l: lacking self-confidence · short
arousing or provoking laughter · beyond or deviating from the usual or expected
moving slowly and gently · disinclined to work or exertion

ejercicios.frase: My new boss is very sympathetic and always smiles.
respuestas: My new boss is very friendly and always smiles.
My new boss is very nice and always smiles.
ejercicios.explicacion: This is the false friend listed among the card's typical mistakes: sympathetic means “understanding, compassionate”, not Spanish “simpático”. The clue is always smiles: it describes someone kind and pleasant, which in English is friendly or nice. Both corrections are valid.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Spanish “simpático” is friendly or nice; sympathetic means understanding.
ejercicios.traduccion: Mi nuevo jefe es muy simpático y siempre sonríe.

errores_previstos.respuesta: My new boss is very sympathetic and always smiles.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: sympathetic means understanding; for “simpático” use friendly or nice.

errores_previstos.respuesta: My new boss is very simpathetic and always smiles.
errores_previstos.explicacion: As well as being the false friend, it is misspelt; the correction is friendly or nice.

errores_previstos.respuesta: My new boss is very funny and always smiles.
errores_previstos.explicacion: Funny means “amusing”, not “kind and pleasant”; the right word is friendly or nice.

glosario.definicion_l: of or relating to the sympathetic nervous system · expressing or feeling or resulting from sympathy or compassion or friendly fellow feelings; disposed toward
exceptionally good · a person who exercises control over workers

ejercicios.frase: She looks like to her grandmother.
ejercicios.explicacion: The second table gives look like: be similar in appearance to. The key point is that look like is followed directly by the person, with no preposition: like already does the job of Spanish “a”. The clue is the sequence like to, a literal translation of Spanish “parecerse a”.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Look like is followed directly by the object, without to.

errores_previstos.respuesta: She looks like to her grandmother.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: look like does not take to.
Without like the meaning changes (look to = rely on); for physical similarity use look like.
With she, the present simple takes -s: looks.

glosario.definicion_l: the mother of your father or mother

ejercicios.frase: My sister has a long hair.
respuestas: My sister has got long hair.
ejercicios.explicacion: The list of rules and key points says that for hair you use have. The key point is that hair, when it means the hair on your head, is uncountable and does not take a. The clue is a long hair: a long hair would be one single long hair. has, 's got and has got are all accepted.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Hair is uncountable when it means the hair on your head: no a.
ejercicios.traduccion: Mi hermana tiene el pelo largo.

errores_previstos.respuesta: My sister has a long hair.
errores_previstos.explicacion: This is the uncorrected sentence: hair (on the head) is uncountable and does not take a.
Hairs are individual, countable hairs; the hair on your head is hair, with no plural.
For hair, use have, not be: She has long hair.

glosario.significado: pelo (incontable cuando es el de la cabeza)
glosario.definicion_l: a covering for the body (or parts of it) consisting of a dense growth of threadlike structures (as on the human head); helps to prevent heat loss · a very small distance or space
primarily temporal sense; being or indicating a relatively great or greater than average duration or passage of time or a duration as specified

respuestas: I get on well with my brother
ejercicios.explicacion: The second table gives get on well with: have a good relationship with. The key point is the order of the phrasal verb: get on, then the adverb well and the preposition with plus the person. The subject I goes first. It is a very common expression for talking about family relationships.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Get on well with means to have a good relationship with someone.
ejercicios.traduccion: Me llevo bien con mi hermano.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I get well on with my brother
errores_previstos.explicacion: Well goes after the particle on: get on well with.

errores_previstos.respuesta: I well get on with my brother
errores_previstos.explicacion: Well does not go before the verb; the fixed expression is get on well with.

glosario.definicion_l: (Roman Catholic Church) a title given to a monk and used as form of address · a male with the same parents as someone else

ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives siblings: brothers and sisters, either sex. The grammatical key point is the present simple question: Do + subject (you) + have + any + plural noun. The clue is do among the words, which goes at the beginning to form the question.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Question with do + subject + have + any.

errores_previstos.explicacion: This is an emphatic statement, not a question; do goes before the subject.
Have goes right after the subject, before any siblings.

glosario.definicion_l: a person's brother or sister

ejercicios.enunciado: Complete: the person you live with (not married).
ejercicios.frase: I live with my ___, but we aren't married.
ejercicios.explicacion: The card's table gives partner (Spanish “pareja”) and boyfriend / girlfriend. The clue is “but we aren't married”: it is a couple who are not married. Partner is the neutral form and the one the instruction asks for; boyfriend and girlfriend are also accepted because they fit the sentence.
ejercicios.traduccion: Vivo con mi pareja, pero no estamos casados.

errores_previstos.explicacion: Couple means two people together (they are a couple); the person you live with is your partner.
Husband means a married man; it contradicts we aren't married.
Pair is used for two objects (a pair of shoes); it is not used for people.

glosario.definicion_l: a person's partner in marriage · an associate in an activity or endeavor or sphere of common interest
a pair who associate with one another · a pair of people who live together
take in marriage; married · perform a marriage ceremony

ejercicios.explicacion: The table gives grandfather / grandmother: the father / mother of a parent. The clue is the relationship: your grandmother's husband is your grandfather. Uncle and father-in-law are different relationships.
ejercicios.explicacion_breve: Your grandmother's husband is your grandfather.
ejercicios.traduccion: El marido de mi abuela es mi abuelo.

por_opcion.uncle: Incorrect: uncle is the brother of your father or mother.
por_opcion.father-in-law: Incorrect: father-in-law is your spouse's father.

glosario.definicion_l: the father of your father or mother
a married man; a woman's partner in marriage · use cautiously and frugally

descripcion_larga_es: This card brings together the basic words for talking about the family (parents, siblings, aunt, cousin, father-in-law), partners and marital status, and for describing a person's appearance and personality. It is one of the first things you need to introduce yourself or have a conversation, and it has traps for Spanish speakers: parents are not “parientes” (relatives), sympathetic is not “simpático” and brothers does not include sisters.

contexto.que_es: It is the vocabulary of family relationships (parents, siblings, grandparents, uncles and aunts, cousins, nephews and nieces, in-laws), partners and marital status, together with the basic adjectives and expressions for describing a person's appearance and personality: tall, fair hair, shy, look like, get on well with.
contexto.por_que_importa: Talking about yourself and the people around you is one of the first tasks in any language: introducing yourself, saying who you live with or describing someone. Some mistakes change the meaning without the speaker noticing (my fathers instead of my parents, brothers for brother and sister), and others are false friends (sympathetic, educated) that can cause misunderstandings.
contexto.cuando_se_usa: It is used when introducing yourself, in informal conversation, when describing someone or when filling in forms (marital status, relationship). The signals are questions such as Do you have any siblings?, What is he like? or What does he look like? Spanish speakers tend to use the masculine plural for both sexes (Spanish “hermanos”, “padres”) and to copy “simpático” or “educado”; English has its own words for these.
